items.label: Let & Const
items.answer: Modern JavaScript introduces `let` and `const` to lock variables into the specific block `{}` where they are declared. This replaces the old `var` keyword, which is function-scoped and hoists variables, leading to silent data mutation bugs.

items.label: Analyze variable hoisting mechanics and the temporal dead zone
items.answer:
Hoisting is JavaScript's default behavior of moving declarations to the top of the current scope before execution phase. While var hoists with an uninitialized value of undefined, modern declarations alter this execution path.

For example:
• Calling a var variable before declaration returns undefined without crashing.
• Calling a let or const variable before its line of declaration throws a ReferenceError.

The Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) is the exact area from the start of the block until the variable is officially declared.

In short: The TDZ protects your application by forcing safe code practices, mandating variables be declared before usage.

items.label: Review template literal backtick string rules and interpolation expressions
items.answer:
Template Literals are string literals enclosed by backtick characters (`) instead of traditional single or double quotes, introducing native embedded evaluation placeholder paths.

For example:
• They allow string interpolation using the exact ${expression} placeholder syntax configuration.
• They support native multi-line layout formatting strings without needing escape characters like \n.
• They compute active JavaScript mathematical operations, conditions, or function returns inline on the fly.

In short: Template literals simplify complex string combinations by executing internal inline expressions cleanly.

Analyze lexical scope this binding inside arrow functions vs normal functions
items.answer: Arrow functions do not bind their own this context; instead, they inherit it lexically from the parent scope.

items.label: Master syntax patterns for object extraction and array pattern destructuring
items.answer: Destructuring allows clean, unpackaged extraction of properties from objects and arrays straight into distinct local variables.

items.label: Differentiate shallow copying spread syntax from parameter gathering rest operations
items.answer: Spread parameters unpack elements out of arrays or objects, while rest syntax groups separate incoming values into one unified array collection wrapper.
